# Copilot Instructions for mahmoud Repository

## Overview
This repository contains instructions and guidelines for GitHub Copilot to follow when generating code suggestions, conducting code reviews, and assisting with development tasks.

## General Guidelines

### Code Quality
- Write clean, readable, and maintainable code
- Follow established best practices for each programming language
- Add comments for complex logic or non-obvious implementations
- Keep functions and methods focused on a single responsibility

### Documentation
- Maintain up-to-date documentation
- Include clear README files for project setup and usage
- Document API endpoints, function parameters, and return values
- Add inline documentation for public interfaces

### Testing
- Write comprehensive tests for new functionality
- Maintain existing test coverage
- Follow the existing testing patterns in the repository
- Include both unit tests and integration tests where appropriate

### Version Control
- Write clear, descriptive commit messages
- Keep commits atomic and focused on a single change
- Follow conventional commit message format when applicable

### Security
- Never commit sensitive information (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- Follow security best practices for the technology stack
- Validate and sanitize all user inputs
- Use secure dependencies and keep them updated

### Performance
- Consider performance implications of code changes
- Optimize for readability first, then performance if needed
- Profile before optimizing
- Document any performance-critical sections

## Project-Specific Guidelines

### Repository Structure
- Maintain a clean and organized directory structure
- Place related files together
- Use meaningful file and directory names

### Code Review
- Be thorough but constructive in code reviews
- Focus on important issues (bugs, security, performance)
- Suggest improvements with clear explanations
- Acknowledge good practices in the code

## Contributing
When suggesting changes or additions:
- Ensure changes are minimal and focused
- Verify changes don't break existing functionality
- Follow the existing code style and patterns
- Test changes before submitting
